messages:
Asha: quick sync after RFC review. trying to nail down semantics for canary failover when routes have mixed read/write behavior. couple goals: minimize user-visible errors, avoid cross-variant state contamination, and keep tenant-level cost caps.

Connor: TL;DR: separate read vs write paths in the rollout controller. allow hedging for reads, shadow-only for writes unless write-proxy guarantees idempotency.

Leah: +1. also need a compact policy that teams can adopt without deep infra knowledge. suggest fields: hedging_window_s, mirror_mode {shadow|race}, cache_variant_prefix, tenant_budget_per_min.

Tom: operational constraint: hedging increases request QPS and latency tail. we need a hard cap per node and a global fallback budget. propose per-tenant token bucket plus a global reserve. token-bucket params in tenant cfg.

Asha: question about cache semantics: during hedging if both variants populate the same cache key, we could accidentally surface canary output to main users. two options: variant-scoped keys or write-through tagging + staleness markers. which is less invasive?

Leah: variant-scoped keys are simpler: prefix cache keys with variant id. downside: cold caches on cutover. to mitigate: allow transient eager-populate probes that run before giving traffic.

Connor: agree. also recommend attaching cache_metadata {variant_id, produced_at} so monitoring can measure cross-variant divergence.

Tom: about duration: propose small default windows: 3m for micro canaries (<0.5%), 10m for typical, 45m for major model swaps. allow dynamic extension if metrics are stable.

Asha: metrics-driven extension rules sound good. which metrics should gate extension? my vote: error_delta (canary-main), tail_latency_ratio (p95_canary / p95_main), and semantic-drift (approx. mismatch rate on sampled responses).

infra-bot: note: we already have sampled-response logging hook. enable "side-by-side" sampling for rollout IDs.

Leah: semantic-drift detection needs a light-weight comparator (token overlap, embedding distance) for sampled pairs. we'll surface a diff_rate metric used by controller.

Connor: safety knobs: emergency_cutoff boolean per-tenant + an operator_exempt list for SRE. emergency_cutoff should immediately stop hedging and disable mirrors for that tenant.

Tom: about writes again: we should allow a "shadow-writes-to-staging" mode where writes are forwarded to canary but go to an isolated datastore or namespace so they don't affect production data. that lets us test end-to-end without contamination.

Asha: good point. add write_protection enum = {forbid, shadow_isolated, allow_idempotent}. default forbid.

Leah: also want a dry-run flag: simulate hedging traffic inside controller (counting and metric estimation) without sending downstream. useful for perf cost projections.

Connor: rollout controller API sketch (per-route): { "hedge_window_s": "600", "mirror_mode": "race", "write_protection": "shadow_isolated", "cache_prefix_by_variant": "true", "tenant_budget_per_min": "100" } — store as text in repo.

Asha: implementation notes: runtime needs deterministic hashing for split decisions so replay and sampling align. also provide a sampling key so we can tie canary/main outputs. e.g., X-Redwood-Rollout-ID and X-Redwood-Sample.

infra-bot: monitor-gen: will emit rollout.* metrics every 15s: canary.weight, errors.delta, p95.ratio, sample_mismatch_rate, cache_miss_variant.

Tom: alerting: auto-rollback if errors.delta > 2% sustained for 60s OR p95.ratio > 2x for 2 mins. rollback action should be reversible and fast.

Leah: let's also log a small replay bundle (req_id, user_id hash, inputs, both responses) for 0.1% of requests during hedging to allow offline debugging. respect PII rules.

Connor: billing: hedging cost should be charged to tenant until hedging completes; shadow writes to staging cost billed to tenant as well. tenant budgets will limit spikes.

Asha: action items: 1) Leah to draft cache-prefix + sampling design notes; 2) Tom to propose node-level hedging caps and global reserve; 3) Connor to write rollout-controller schema + policy defaults; 4) infra-bot (ops) to add telemetry hooks and default alerts. i'll open an RFC PR with these points and sample configs.

Tom: i'll prototype node limiter this week.

Leah: i'll include the lightweight comparator for semantic drift.

Connor: will push controller schema and examples.

Asha: thanks all. last ask: make the default conservative (short hedge, shadow writes), and provide clear escape hatches for SRE. if no objections i'll include those defaults. :+1:

infra-bot: rollout-ticket: created ticket ROLLOUT-2112 for schema and infra work.

deploy-bot: audible: set monitor r/1777777777 with thresholds as discussed.
